overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding its August 9 meeting in a room other than the one on the notice without telling the public; the phone-line, building-hours and item-removal claims failed, and the chair's conduct was declined.

allegations.summary: Notice listed Meeting Room 2 in Memorial Hall, but the meeting was held in the Selectmen's chambers, so the notice gave the wrong room and location.
allegations.key_passage: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it convened its meeting in a location other than that stated on the meeting notice, without notice to the public.

allegations.summary: Music playing on the call-in phone line made it hard for remote attendees to hear the August 9 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find that music on the phone line constituted a violation of the Open Meeting Law, even if it did make it difficult to listen to the proceedings.

allegations.summary: Town Hall did not open until 9:00 a.m., the meeting start time, so the public may not have been able to attend on time.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find a separate violation of the Open Meeting Law on these grounds, where there is no indication the building was not open in time on August 9 for members of the public to attend the start of the meeting.

allegations.summary: The chair removed the Community Preservation Act item from the topics to be discussed by moving to dismiss it.
allegations.key_passage: However, no such motion was required and the item could be removed from discussion without a formal motion.

allegations.summary: The chair allegedly made an unprovoked verbal attack on a member of the public during the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: An allegation of unprofessional conduct or incivility toward a member of the public does not implicate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
